summary: Reddit, X and Bluesky were unreachable, so today's themes come from Hacker News threads only. The strongest: scam checkouts and unreadable card statements after a delivery-site skimming campaign, small firms fleeing QuickBooks price hikes, and frustration with Apple's keyboard and with chat apps families won't adopt.

ideas.title: Statement Decoder: what did I actually buy?
ideas.oneLiner: Turns cryptic card/UPI statement lines into the real merchant and order by matching them against your email and SMS receipts.
ideas.problem: Small restaurants and shops charge through processors whose names look nothing like the business, so people can't tell a legitimate charge from fraud on their statement. Users want processors to expose more detail, but that won't happen soon.
ideas.targetUsers: Anyone who reviews card or UPI statements: families, freelancers and small-business owners reconciling spending, and people who've been hit by a scam charge.
ideas.monetization: Free for 30 days of history; ₹99/month or ₹799/year for unlimited history, export to CSV, and shared household view.
mvp: On-device parsing of bank/UPI SMS and notification text (Android) to pull amount, date and descriptor
Match each charge to receipts in Gmail (read-only) by amount and date
Crowd-sourced descriptor dictionary ('RZP*ACME FOODS' → 'Acme Biryani, Koramangala')
'Unrecognised charge' inbox with one-tap 'ask my family' share
Monthly CSV export

competitors.name: Walnut / Money Manager style SMS expense trackers
competitors.gap: Categorise spend but show the raw descriptor; no matching to the receipt that explains it.

competitors.name: Bank apps
competitors.gap: Show one line per transaction and offer no processor or order detail.

competitors.name: Rocket Money / Mint-style apps
competitors.gap: US-centric, no Indian UPI or SMS coverage, and descriptor cleaning is shallow.

ideas.title: Real Checkout: verify the site before you pay
ideas.oneLiner: A checkout guard that tells you whether the page asking for your card is actually run by the business you meant to order from.
ideas.problem: Scam sites buy search ads that outrank the real business, and legitimate businesses hand payments to generic, unfamiliar-looking domains, so users can't tell the two apart. Reporting scams to Google or Meta rarely gets results.
ideas.targetUsers: Everyday shoppers and food-delivery users, especially less technical family members; local restaurants who get complaint calls from scam victims.
ideas.monetization: Free for individuals; ₹199/month per business for a verified-domain listing and takedown alerts; family plan ₹49/month.
mvp: Detect payment-form pages and show a green/amber/red banner before card entry
Check domain age, lookalike TLDs (.delivery, .shop) and ad-click referrals against known brand domains
Business-claimed domain registry plus known payment-processor allowlist (so legitimate id.me-style hops aren't flagged)
One-tap 'report this site' that files abuse reports with the registrar, host and Google Safe Browsing
Warning shown when you reach a checkout from a search ad

competitors.name: Google Safe Browsing
competitors.gap: Reactive blocklist; scam domains rotate faster than they are listed, and scam ads still run.

competitors.name: ScamAdviser / Norton Genie
competitors.gap: Generic trust scores, nothing that says whether this is the restaurant you meant to order from.

competitors.name: Bank card-on-file alerts
competitors.gap: Fire after the money has moved.

ideas.title: Plain Books: a QuickBooks escape for tiny firms
ideas.oneLiner: Simple bookkeeping for 1–10 person firms: import bank transactions, auto-categorise, and hand your accountant a clean export.
ideas.problem: Small firm owners are unhappy with repeated QuickBooks price rises and a desktop-versus-online split with different features, but want something their accountant can still work with.
ideas.targetUsers: Solo professionals and small firms (law, consulting, clinics, agencies) and their part-time bookkeepers or CAs.
ideas.monetization: ₹499–₹1,499/month per firm with unlimited users; accountant seats free to drive referrals.
mvp: Bank/credit-card CSV and statement import with rule-based plus LLM-assisted categorisation
Review queue that flags low-confidence categories instead of silently guessing
Invoices, receipts attachment and simple P&L / balance sheet
Accountant export in formats QuickBooks, Tally and Zoho Books can import
Read-only accountant share link

competitors.name: QuickBooks
competitors.gap: Frequent price increases; online and desktop editions lack feature parity.

competitors.name: Wave
competitors.gap: Light on categorisation help and accountant workflow for firms with several users.

competitors.name: Zoho Books / Xero
competitors.gap: Capable but priced and structured for growing companies, with heavy setup for a three-person firm.

competitors.name: GnuCash
competitors.gap: Free and solid but desktop-only with a steep learning curve and no collaboration.

ideas.title: Hearth: a family chat app on your own server
ideas.oneLiner: A dead-simple private family messenger: you run a tiny server in one click, relatives join from an invite link, and it feels like WhatsApp.
ideas.problem: Technical people want to move their families off SMS and WhatsApp, but Matrix and XMPP clients are widely described as clunky or unreliable, and the iOS experience is a known weak spot.
ideas.targetUsers: Privacy-minded parents and the relatives they'd have to convince; homelab hobbyists who gave up on Matrix.
ideas.monetization: Hosted family server ₹299/month (up to 10 members); self-host build free; one-time ₹499 to unlock extra storage and backups.
mvp: Flutter client for Android and iOS with only 1:1, family group, photos and voice notes
One-click server deploy (managed hosting, or a script for a small VPS)
Invite by link/QR with no email or phone number needed
Reliable push notifications on both platforms
Encrypted backup and restore to a new phone

competitors.name: Snikket
competitors.gap: Closest in spirit, but its maintainer says the iOS app is a known weak point and there's no full web client yet.

competitors.name: Element / Matrix
competitors.gap: Commenters call the clients some of the worst they've used.

competitors.name: Delta Chat
competitors.gap: Praised for UX and reliability, but built on email so it needs a chatmail server and isn't instant-feeling for some.

ideas.title: Plain Keys: a predictable iPhone keyboard
ideas.oneLiner: An iOS keyboard with fixed key sizes, no hidden word blocklist, and a dictionary that only learns what you tell it to.
ideas.problem: iPhone users say Apple's keyboard got worse, from autocorrect misfires to invisibly resized touch targets, and many just switch autocorrect off. Technical typists are especially annoyed.
ideas.targetUsers: iPhone users who type a lot, including developers, writers and people typing in two or more languages.
ideas.monetization: Free basic keyboard; ₹149/month or ₹999 lifetime for custom dictionaries, snippets, multilingual packs and iCloud sync.
mvp: Fixed-size key hit areas with a visible touch-target overlay for debugging
Autocorrect off by default, with an opt-in 'fix only obvious typos' mode
User-owned dictionary and phrase list, exportable
Swipe typing with on-device-only models
Technical mode that doesn't mangle code, URLs, and mixed-language text

competitors.name: Gboard for iOS
competitors.gap: Sends typed data through Google services and has limited deep customisation.

competitors.name: SwiftKey
competitors.gap: Microsoft account sync and cloud prediction, which privacy-minded users avoid.

competitors.name: Typewise
competitors.gap: Different layout that takes relearning rather than fixing predictability.

ideas.title: Tube Lifeboat: playlists and feeds that don't rot
ideas.oneLiner: Backs up your YouTube subscriptions and playlist metadata, tells you when videos vanish, and keeps your feed working when YouTube RSS breaks.
ideas.problem: Long-time YouTube users watch their saved playlists fill with 'unavailable' entries they can't identify, and RSS-based subscribers just had channel feeds return 404 for days.
ideas.targetUsers: Heavy YouTube curators and RSS/feed-reader users who follow channels outside the algorithm.
ideas.monetization: Free for 3 playlists; ₹149/month for unlimited playlists, daily snapshots, feed fallback and OPML export.
mvp: Google sign-in with read-only playlist and subscription import
Nightly snapshot of titles, channels and thumbnails so removed videos can still be identified
'What disappeared' diff view with Wayback/other-source search links
Fallback feed built from channel pages when official RSS 404s
OPML and JSON export

competitors.name: RSS-Bridge / FreshRSS
competitors.gap: Self-hosted and technical; they depend on the same endpoints that just broke.

competitors.name: Invidious / Piped
competitors.gap: Instances are often rate-limited or blocked, and they don't track your playlist history.

competitors.name: Playlist backup extensions
competitors.gap: One-off exports that don't monitor for changes or fix feeds.

ideas.title: Already Own It: recommendations that respect your history
ideas.oneLiner: Hides shop and store recommendations for things you've already bought, finished, rated badly or dismissed.
ideas.problem: People are tired of being shown items they already bought, sequels to books they never finished or 1-starred, and feeds that herd them into a few genres, despite the platforms holding that data.
ideas.targetUsers: Frequent Amazon/Kindle shoppers and heavy music or book consumers who want recommendations without the repeats.
ideas.monetization: Free for one store; ₹99/month or ₹699 lifetime for all supported stores and cross-device sync.
mvp: Import order history from Amazon (CSV/page scrape) once
Hide already-purchased items and listed series entries in carousels and search
Hide items from authors/series you've rated 1–2 stars or marked dismissed
Local-only storage, no server
Toggle to show hidden items

competitors.name: Amazon 'Not interested' / manage recommendations
competitors.gap: Manual item-by-item, and repeats still appear.

competitors.name: uBlock Origin cosmetic filters
competitors.gap: Needs hand-written rules and knows nothing about your purchase history.

competitors.name: Goodreads
competitors.gap: Tracks reading but doesn't affect what Amazon shows you.

ideas.title: Shotwise: turn screenshot graveyards into notes
ideas.oneLiner: Reads your screenshots on-device, pulls out the useful bit (link, recipe, address, receipt) and files it somewhere you can search.
ideas.problem: People save screenshots and bookmarks 'for later', then can't find them. Galleries fill with thousands of images of which only a few percent are ever used.
ideas.targetUsers: Heavy phone screenshotters, researchers and students who save things for later and rarely revisit them.
ideas.monetization: Free for 100 screenshots; ₹99/month or ₹799/year for unlimited, reminders and export to Notion/Obsidian.
mvp: Auto-detect new screenshots and run on-device OCR
Classify into link, recipe, address, receipt, quote or other, and extract the key fields
Searchable inbox with 'resurface in a week' reminders
Auto-archive screenshots with no extracted value
Export to Notion, Obsidian or plain Markdown

competitors.name: Google Photos / Apple Photos search
competitors.gap: OCR search exists but nothing is extracted or resurfaced, so screenshots stay a graveyard.

competitors.name: Karakeep / Linkding / Zotero
competitors.gap: Commenters call the UIs dated or rough, and they don't ingest screenshots.

competitors.name: Pocket-style read-later apps
competitors.gap: Handle links only, not screenshots of apps, chats and recipes.
